sentence_stem: By the time the train arrives,
correct_completion: we will have been waiting for two hours.
full_sentence: By the time the train arrives, we will have been waiting for two hours.
acceptable_variants: we will have been standing on this platform for two hours.
we will have spent two hours waiting.

options.text: we are waiting for two hours now.
options.why_wrong: The present continuous describes the current moment, but the stem needs a future time reference with an activity completed up to that point.

options.text: we will have been waiting for two hours.
we waited for two hours yesterday.
options.why_wrong: The past simple refers to a finished past event and does not fit the future time reference set by 'by the time'.

options.text: we will wait for two hours.
options.why_wrong: The simple future describes a future action but does not show it continuing up to the moment the train arrives, which the future perfect continuous conveys.

grammar_focus: Future perfect continuous with 'by the time' and a present tense in the time clause
explanation: The future perfect continuous describes an activity that will still be in progress up to a future point, here marked by 'by the time'. The time clause uses the present simple even though it refers to the future. Polish speakers often use a simple future in this position because Polish expresses completion through verb aspect rather than a separate auxiliary, so the English progressive perfect structure needs deliberate practice.
translation: Do czasu, gdy pociąg przyjedzie, będziemy już czekać dwie godziny.
